summary: This Wikipedia article explains the national debt of the United States, defined as the face value of outstanding Treasury securities owed to holders, and distinguishes debt held by the public from intragovernmental debt. It traces historical debt levels relative to GDP from 1789 onward, notes recent record totals and the rising CBO projections, and covers budget deficits, foreign holdings, and the 2018 debt issuance surge, along with valuation and measurement issues. The page as captured is partial, ending in its valuation section.
one_line: Overview of the U.S. federal national debt: its definition, components, historical trends, recent totals, and projections.
key_facts: The national debt of the United States is the total national debt owed by the federal government to Treasury security holders, measured as the face value of outstanding Treasury securities issued by the Treasury and other federal agencies.
Gross national debt has two components: debt held by the public and debt held by government accounts (intragovernmental debt).

The federal government has continuously had a fluctuating public debt since its formation in 1789, except for about a year during 1835–1836, when President Andrew Jackson's administration completely paid the national debt.
Public debt as a percentage of GDP reached its highest level during Harry Truman's first presidential term, during and after World War II, and reached a low in 1974 under Richard Nixon.
The Congressional Budget Office estimated in February 2024 that federal debt held by the public would rise from 99 percent of GDP in 2024 to 116 percent in 2034, and to 172 percent of GDP in 2054.
Total US federal government debt breached the $30 trillion mark for the first time in February 2022.
As of December 2023, total federal debt was $33.1 trillion: $26.5 trillion held by the public and $12.1 trillion in intragovernmental debt.
In February 2024, total federal government debt grew to $34.4 trillion.
The annualized cost of servicing the debt was $726 billion in July 2023, accounting for 14% of total federal spending.
In December 2021, debt held by the public was estimated at 96.19% of GDP, and approximately 33% of this public debt was owned by foreigners.
The CBO estimated that the budget deficit for fiscal year 2020 would increase to $3.3 trillion or 16% of GDP, more than triple that of 2019 and the largest as a percentage of GDP since 1945.
The CBO estimated the federal budget deficit for fiscal year 2018 was c.$782 billion, which is $116 billion more than in FY2017.
As of July 20, 2020, debt held by the public was $20.57 trillion and intragovernmental holdings were $5.94 trillion, for a total of $26.51 trillion.
Debt held by the public was approximately 77% of GDP in 2017, ranked 43rd highest out of 207 countries.
Public debt rose sharply during the 1980s under Ronald Reagan, and fell during the 1990s due to decreased military spending, increased taxes and the 1990s boom.
